# Run all chunks from the repo root, so paths match the repo layout
# (data/..., analysis/...) whether knitted from RStudio or from a script.
repo <- system("git rev-parse --show-toplevel", intern = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = repo)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(ape)

# Fetch input files that are not yet in data/, in one call to the shared
# downloader (scripts/download_files.sh, see CLAUDE.md).
fetch <- function(paths) {
  missing <- paths[!file.exists(file.path(repo, paths))]
  if (length(missing) > 0) {
    status <- system2(file.path(repo, "scripts/download_files.sh"), shQuote(missing))
    if (status != 0) stop("Download failed for: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
  }
  invisible(paths)
}

# Figure and table numbers, in order of appearance
fig_ids <- c("landscape", "genes_dups", "sd_contig", "nb_scheme", "anc_branches", "nb_events",
             "ks_heat", "anc_ks", "summary")
tab_ids <- c("orders", "nb_calib", "anc_counts", "peaks", "orthks", "anc")
fig  <- function(id) paste("Figure", match(id, fig_ids))
tab  <- function(id) paste("Table", match(id, tab_ids))
cap  <- function(id, text) paste0("**", fig(id), ".** ", text)
tcap <- function(id, text) paste0(tab(id), ". ", text)

order_levels <- c("Mortierellales", "Umbelopsidales", "Mucorales")
order_cols <- c(Mortierellales = "#E69F00", Umbelopsidales = "#009E73", Mucorales = "#0072B2")
mode_levels <- c("SD", "TD", "PD", "DD", "Near-identical")
mode_labs <- c(SD = "Segmental (SD)", TD = "Tandem (TD)", PD = "Proximal (PD)",
               DD = "Dispersed (DD)", "Near-identical" = "Near-identical (Ks < 0.05 or missing)")
mode_cols <- c(SD = "#D55E00", TD = "#CC79A7", PD = "#56B4E9", DD = "grey70",
               "Near-identical" = "grey20")
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 10) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

pct <- function(x, digits = 0) format(round(100 * x, digits), nsmall = digits)
fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
```

# Overview {-}

Duplicated genes were classified in 61 genomes of Mortierellales,
Umbelopsidales and Mucorales, compared across genomes, and traced back to the
branches of the species tree where they arose. Because gene order is scrambled
in many of these genomes, duplications that arose in blocks were identified
with a measure of synteny that does not depend on gene order, and their Ks
distributions were used to date the large-scale duplication events. The
extended analyses behind this report (assembly QC, gene-tree duplication rates,
macrosynteny, copy-number tests, robustness checks) are in
[`wgd_mucoromycota.Rmd`](wgd_mucoromycota.Rmd).

```{r data}
fetch(c("data/metadata/genome_metadata_master.csv",
        "data/metadata/assembly_qc_summary.csv",
        "data/phylogeny/sco_cds_b500.date.nwk",
        "data/orthofinder/results/Comparative_Genomics_Statistics/Statistics_PerSpecies.tsv"))

md <- fread("data/metadata/genome_metadata_master.csv")
gen <- md[include_core_analyses == "yes",
          .(genome = tree_label, dt_id = genome_id, species = species_name, family,
            order = factor(order, order_levels))]
tree <- read.tree("data/phylogeny/sco_cds_b500.date.nwk")
stopifnot(setequal(gen$genome, tree$tip.label), !anyNA(gen$order))

# Number of protein-coding genes (OrthoFinder input proteomes)
ps <- fread("data/orthofinder/results/Comparative_Genomics_Statistics/Statistics_PerSpecies.tsv",
            header = TRUE, nrows = 10)
setnames(ps, 1, "stat")
ng <- unlist(ps[stat == "Number of genes", -1])
# OrthoFinder species names (e.g. AbsRepe_prot, gzAbsCyli1.proteins) by genome
of_names <- setNames(names(ng), sub("[._](prot|proteins|pep)$", "", names(ng)))
names(ng) <- names(of_names)
gen[, genes := as.numeric(ng[genome])]
stopifnot(!anyNA(gen$genes))

qc <- fread("data/metadata/assembly_qc_summary.csv")
gen[, busco_dup := qc$Busco_Dup[match(genome, qc$genome_id)]]

# Genomes in tree order (bottom to top), for plots
tip_data <- ggtree(tree)$data
tip_order <- with(tip_data[tip_data$isTip, ], label[order(y)])
```

```{r contig-lengths}
# Sequence lengths of every assembly. Computed once on NeLS (awk over each
# assembly FASTA, so the ~3 GB of assemblies are not downloaded) and saved to
# data/. This is the one NeLS-specific step; at publication the table is
# deposited with the other data files.
cl_path <- "data/genome_duplication/contig_lengths.tsv"
if (!file.exists(cl_path)) {
  remote <- paste(
    "cd", shQuote(nels_path("data/genomes")), "&& printf 'genome\\tseqname\\tlength\\n' &&",
    "for g in *; do",
    "f=$(ls \"$g\" | grep -E '\\.(fna|fasta|fa|fas)(\\.gz)?$' | grep -viE 'cds|transcript|protein|rna_from');",
    "[ $(echo $f | wc -w) -eq 1 ] || { echo \"No unique assembly in $g\" >&2; exit 1; };",
    "case \"$f\" in *.gz) r='gzip -dc';; *) r=cat;; esac;",
    "$r \"$g/$f\" | awk -v g=\"$g\" '/^>/ {if (n != \"\") print g \"\\t\" n \"\\t\" l; n = substr($1, 2); l = 0; next}",
    "{l += length($0)} END {if (n != \"\") print g \"\\t\" n \"\\t\" l}';",
    "done")
  dir.create(dirname(cl_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  writeLines(.nels_run(remote), cl_path)
}
cl <- fread(cl_path, colClasses = c(seqname = "character"))
stopifnot(all(gen$genome %in% cl$genome))
```

```{r gene-positions}
fetch(sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_genePosTbl.tsv", gen$genome))
gp <- rbindlist(lapply(gen$genome, function(g) {
  fread(sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_genePosTbl.tsv", g),
        colClasses = c(seqname = "character"))[, genome := g]
}))
gp <- merge(gp, cl, by = c("genome", "seqname"), all.x = TRUE)
stopifnot(mean(!is.na(gp$length)) > 0.99)  # gene tables and assemblies use the same names
```

```{r doubletrouble}
dup_files  <- sprintf("data/doubletrouble/dups/%s_dup.rds", gen$dt_id)
kaks_files <- sprintf("data/doubletrouble/kaks/%s_kaks.rds", gen$dt_id)
fetch(c(dup_files, kaks_files))

pairs <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(gen)), function(i) {
  d <- as.data.table(readRDS(dup_files[i]))
  k <- as.data.table(readRDS(kaks_files[i])[[1]])
  d <- merge(d, k[, .(dup1, dup2, Ka, Ks)], by = c("dup1", "dup2"), all.x = TRUE)
  d[, .(genome = gen$genome[i], dup1, dup2, type = as.character(type),
        seq1 = as.character(seqname1), seq2 = as.character(seqname2), Ka, Ks)]
}))
# Near-identical pairs: Ks < 0.05, or Ks not estimable (mostly identical
# sequences, see Section 1.2). These are recent duplicates or assembly
# duplicates and are kept apart from the older pairs.
pairs[, near_ident := is.na(Ks) | Ks < 0.05]
```

```{r contiguity-calc}
n50 <- function(x) { x <- sort(x, decreasing = TRUE); x[which(cumsum(x) >= sum(x) / 2)[1]] }
asm <- cl[, .(n_seq = .N, size_mb = sum(length) / 1e6, n50_mb = n50(length) / 1e6), by = genome]
gcont <- gp[, .(gene_seqs = uniqueN(seqname), on_1mb = mean(length >= 1e6, na.rm = TRUE)),
            by = genome]
gen <- merge(gen, asm, by = "genome", all.x = TRUE)
gen <- merge(gen, gcont, by = "genome", all.x = TRUE)
```

```{r nearident-calc}
ni <- pairs[near_ident == TRUE]
ni_sd <- ni[type == "SD", .(ni_sd = .N, ni_sd_seq_pairs = uniqueN(paste(pmin(seq1, seq2), pmax(seq1, seq2)))),
            by = genome]
gen <- merge(gen, ni_sd, by = "genome", all.x = TRUE)
gen[is.na(ni_sd), `:=`(ni_sd = 0L, ni_sd_seq_pairs = 0L)]
gen <- merge(gen, pairs[, .(pairs = .N, ni_all = sum(near_ident),
                            sd_old = sum(type == "SD" & !near_ident)), by = genome],
             by = "genome")
```

# Classifying duplicated genes

Duplicate gene pairs were identified and classified within each genome with
doubletrouble 1.8.1 (standard scheme, default parameters):

- **Paralogous pairs:** each proteome against itself with DIAMOND (top 5 hits
  per protein, E-value <= 1e-10).
- **SD, segmental:** anchor pairs of collinear blocks within the genome
  (MCScanX algorithm in syntenet; at least 5 anchors, up to 25 genes apart).
- **TD, tandem:** remaining pairs that are adjacent on the same sequence.
- **PD, proximal:** remaining pairs 1 to 9 genes apart on the same sequence.
- **DD, dispersed:** all other pairs.
- **Ks:** pairwise codon alignments, MYN model (KaKs_Calculator via MSA2dist).

Pairs with Ks < 0.05 or no estimable Ks (mostly identical sequences) are kept
apart as *near-identical*: they are very recent duplicates or duplicated
stretches of an assembly. Each duplicated gene was given one mode, in the
order SD > TD > PD > DD (`r fig("landscape")`).

```{r gene-modes}
gpairs <- rbind(pairs[, .(genome, gene = dup1, type, near_ident)],
                pairs[, .(genome, gene = dup2, type, near_ident)])
gpairs[, mode := fifelse(near_ident, "Near-identical", type)]
gpairs[, rank := match(mode, mode_levels)]
gmode <- gpairs[, .(mode = mode[which.min(rank)]), by = .(genome, gene)]
land <- gmode[, .N, by = .(genome, mode)]
land <- merge(land, gen[, .(genome, genes, order)], by = "genome")
land[, pct := 100 * N / genes]
land_wide <- dcast(land, genome + order + genes ~ mode, value.var = "pct", fill = 0)
for (m in mode_levels) if (!m %in% names(land_wide)) land_wide[, (m) := 0]
land_wide[, dup_pct := SD + TD + PD + DD]
```

```{r landscape-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10, fig.cap = cap("landscape", "Duplicated genes per genome on the dated species tree. Middle: percentage of genes in each duplication mode (each gene counted once, priority SD > TD > PD > DD; near-identical only for genes in no older pair). Right: number of protein-coding genes. Tip colour: order.")}
tip_df <- data.frame(label = gen$genome, order = gen$order)
p_tree <- ggtree(tree) %<+% tip_df +
  geom_tippoint(aes(colour = order), size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = order_cols, name = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p_modes <- ggplot(land[, .(genome, mode = factor(mode, rev(mode_levels)), pct)],
                  aes(pct, genome, fill = mode)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = mode_cols, labels = mode_labs, name = NULL, breaks = mode_levels) +
  labs(x = "Genes (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
p_genes <- ggplot(gen, aes(genes / 1000, genome, fill = order)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = order_cols) +
  labs(x = "Genes (thousands)", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
p_modes %>% insert_left(p_tree, width = 0.5) %>% insert_right(p_genes, width = 0.35)
```

# Differences across genomes

```{r orders-table}
ord_tab <- land_wide[, .(genomes = .N,
                         genes = median(genes),
                         duplicated = median(dup_pct), SD = median(SD), TD = median(TD),
                         PD = median(PD), DD = median(DD), near_identical = median(`Near-identical`)),
                     by = order][order(order)]
num <- names(ord_tab)[sapply(ord_tab, is.numeric)]
ord_tab[, (num) := lapply(.SD, round, 1), .SDcols = num]
knitr::kable(ord_tab, caption = tcap("orders", "Median number of genes and median percentage of genes in each duplication mode, per order."))
```

```{r genes-dups-fig, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = cap("genes_dups", "Duplicated genes (excluding near-identical) against the number of genes, per duplication mode and in total. Each point is a genome.")}
dup_counts <- dcast(land, genome + order + genes ~ mode, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
for (m in mode_levels) if (!m %in% names(dup_counts)) dup_counts[, (m) := 0]
dup_counts[, All := SD + TD + PD + DD]
dlong <- melt(dup_counts, id.vars = c("genome", "order", "genes"),
              measure.vars = c("All", "SD", "TD", "PD", "DD"), variable.name = "mode", value.name = "dup_genes")
dlong[, mode := factor(mode, c("All", "SD", "TD", "PD", "DD"),
                       c("All modes", mode_labs[c("SD", "TD", "PD", "DD")]))]
ggplot(dlong, aes(genes / 1000, dup_genes / 1000)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = order), size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~mode, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = order_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Genes (thousands)", y = "Duplicated genes (thousands)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

`r round(min(land_wide$dup_pct))`-`r round(max(land_wide$dup_pct))`% of the
genes of each genome are in a paralogous pair, most of them dispersed
(`r tab("orders")`). The total is similar in the three orders, but its make-up
differs: Mortierellales have more segmental, tandem and proximal duplicates and
fewer dispersed ones than Mucorales with the same number of genes
(`r fig("genes_dups")`). Genomes with more genes have more duplicated genes,
mostly dispersed ones.

# Segmental duplicates are concentrated in a few lineages

```{r sd-contig-fig, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = cap("sd_contig", "Segmental duplicate pairs (Ks >= 0.05) per 1,000 genes against the percentage of genes on sequences of at least 1 Mb, where collinear blocks can be detected. Each point is a genome; genomes with more than 20 pairs per 1,000 genes are labelled.")}
gen[, sd_per_1k := 1000 * sd_old / genes]
ggplot(gen, aes(100 * on_1mb, sd_per_1k, colour = order)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_text_repel(data = gen[sd_per_1k > 20], aes(label = genome), size = 3,
                  show.legend = FALSE, max.overlaps = 30) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = order_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Genes on sequences >= 1 Mb (%)", y = "SD pairs (Ks >= 0.05) per 1,000 genes")
```

```{r sd-contig-stats}
# Well-assembled genomes: at least 75% of genes on sequences >= 1 Mb. (The
# Umbelopsidales genomes are small, with chromosomes of 1-2 Mb, so a stricter
# cutoff would exclude all of them.)
hi_cont <- gen[on_1mb >= 0.75]
sd_by_order_hi <- hi_cont[, .(n = .N, median_sd_per_1k = median(sd_per_1k)), by = order][order(order)]
# Share of segmental pairs that are near-identical, per order
sd_ni_share <- pairs[type == "SD"][gen[, .(genome, order)], on = "genome", nomatch = NULL][
  , .(share = mean(near_ident)), by = .(genome, order)][, .(median_share = median(share)), by = order]
```

Among the `r nrow(hi_cont)` well-assembled genomes (at least 75% of genes on
sequences of 1 Mb or more), segmental duplicates are common in Mortierellales
(median `r round(sd_by_order_hi[order == "Mortierellales", median_sd_per_1k], 1)`
pairs per 1,000 genes) and in *Absidia* and *Rhizopus*, and rare in the other
Mucorales (`r round(sd_by_order_hi[order == "Mucorales", median_sd_per_1k], 1)`)
and in Umbelopsidales
(`r round(sd_by_order_hi[order == "Umbelopsidales", median_sd_per_1k], 1)`;
`r fig("sd_contig")`). Their scarcity is therefore not an assembly artifact.
In Mucorales, a median `r pct(sd_ni_share[order == "Mucorales", median_share])`%
of segmental pairs per genome are near-identical, against
`r pct(sd_ni_share[order == "Mortierellales", median_share])`% in
Mortierellales; most extreme is gzMucFlav4, with
`r gen[genome == "gzMucFlav4", fmt_n(ni_sd)]` near-identical segmental pairs
that point to duplicated (uncollapsed haplotype) sequences in its assembly.

# Ancestral segmental duplications

## Why collinearity misses old segmental duplicates

A pair is segmental only if it lies in a collinear block of at least five
pairs in the same order. Gene order within chromosomes is scrambled much faster
in Mucorales and Umbelopsidales than in Mortierellales (synteny analysis), so
blocks from old segmental duplications or WGDs break into pieces too short for
this rule, and their pairs are classified as dispersed even though the
duplicated regions still share genes. The same ancestral duplication can then
be segmental in one genome and dispersed in another.

## Duplications on the species tree

Each OrthoFinder gene-tree duplication with at least 50% support (both copies
retained in at least half of the descendant species) was assigned to the
species-tree branch on which it happened. Within each descendant genome, the
pairs of genes across its two copies were matched to the doubletrouble pairs.

```{r s4-nodes}
fetch(c("data/orthofinder/results/Species_Tree/SpeciesTree_rooted_node_labels.txt",
        "data/orthofinder/results/Gene_Duplication_Events/Duplications.tsv",
        "data/orthofinder/results/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.GeneCount.tsv"))
of_suffix <- "[._](prot|proteins|pep)$"
of_tree <- read.tree("data/orthofinder/results/Species_Tree/SpeciesTree_rooted_node_labels.txt")
of_tree$tip.label <- sub(of_suffix, "", of_tree$tip.label)
nt <- Ntip(of_tree)
depth <- node.depth.edgelength(tree)
root_age <- max(depth)

# OrthoFinder nodes within the 61 core genomes, matched to the dated tree by
# their descendant genomes (nodes where the two topologies differ get no match)
nodes <- rbindlist(lapply(c(seq_len(nt), nt + seq_len(of_tree$Nnode)), function(i) {
  tl <- if (i <= nt) of_tree$tip.label[i] else extract.clade(of_tree, i)$tip.label
  if (!all(tl %in% tree$tip.label)) return(NULL)
  m <- if (length(tl) == 1) match(tl, tree$tip.label) else getMRCA(tree, tl)
  if (length(tl) > 1 && !setequal(extract.clade(tree, m)$tip.label, tl)) m <- NA_integer_
  ords <- unique(as.character(gen$order[match(tl, gen$genome)]))
  data.table(node = if (i <= nt) tl else of_tree$node.label[i - nt], ntips = length(tl),
             dt_node = m, clade_order = if (length(ords) == 1) ords else "Several orders")
}))
nodes[, brlen := tree$edge.length[match(dt_node, tree$edge[, 2])]]
nodes[, age_end := root_age - depth[dt_node]]
nodes[, age_start := age_end + brlen]

dups <- fread("data/orthofinder/results/Gene_Duplication_Events/Duplications.tsv")
setnames(dups, c("og", "of_node", "gt_node", "support", "dup_type", "genes1", "genes2"))
dups[, node := sub(of_suffix, "", of_node)]
sup <- dups[support >= 0.5 & node %in% nodes$node]
nodes <- merge(nodes, sup[, .(dups = .N, ogs = uniqueN(og), single = mean(table(og) == 1)), by = node],
               by = "node", all.x = TRUE)
nodes[is.na(dups), `:=`(dups = 0L, ogs = 0L)]
nodes[, `:=`(rate = dups / brlen, per_og = dups / ogs)]

key_nodes <- data.table(
  node = c("N8", "N9", "N12", "N11", "N10", "N40", "N46", "N32"),
  label = c("Mucoromycota (root)", "Umbelopsidales + Mucorales", "Mucorales", "Umbelopsidales",
            "Mortierellales", "Absidia (3 species)", "A. cylindrospora + A. repens",
            "R. oryzae + R. stolonifer"))
# Internal branches long enough for a rate (very short branches between
# strains of one species give meaningless rates)
internal <- nodes[ntips > 1 & !is.na(brlen) & brlen >= 5]
med_rate <- median(internal$rate)
internal[, rate_rank := frank(-rate)]
```

```{r dup-genes}
fetch(sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_IDtbl.tsv", gen$genome))
alias_all <- rbindlist(lapply(gen$genome, function(g) {
  ids <- fread(sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_IDtbl.tsv", g))
  unique(rbind(ids[, .(id = proteinID, gene = geneID)], ids[, .(id = rnaID, gene = geneID)],
               ids[, .(id = geneID, gene = geneID)]))[, genome := g]
}))
# OrthoFinder writes genes as "<species>_<FASTA header>", with "." in the
# species name replaced by "_", separated by ", ". Pieces without a core-genome
# prefix are outgroup genes or parts of FASTA descriptions that contained ", ".
prefix <- data.table(genome = gen$genome, prefix = paste0(gsub(".", "_", of_names[gen$genome], fixed = TRUE), "_"))
sup_int <- sup[node %in% nodes[ntips > 1, node]]
sup_int[, event := .I]
gl <- rbind(sup_int[, .(event, node, side = 1L, x = genes1)], sup_int[, .(event, node, side = 2L, x = genes2)])
gl <- gl[, .(part = unlist(strsplit(x, ", ", fixed = TRUE))), by = .(event, node, side)]
gl[, genome := NA_character_]
for (i in seq_len(nrow(prefix))) gl[is.na(genome) & startsWith(part, prefix$prefix[i]), genome := prefix$genome[i]]
gl <- gl[!is.na(genome)]
gl[, id := sub(" .*", "", substring(part, nchar(prefix$prefix[match(genome, prefix$genome)]) + 1))]
gl <- merge(gl, alias_all, by = c("genome", "id"), all.x = TRUE)
gene_map_rate <- mean(!is.na(gl$gene))
gl <- gl[!is.na(gene)]

cross <- merge(gl[side == 1, .(event, node, genome, g1 = gene)], gl[side == 2, .(event, genome, g2 = gene)],
               by = c("event", "genome"), allow.cartesian = TRUE)
cross[, key := paste(pmin(g1, g2), pmax(g1, g2))]
cross <- unique(cross, by = c("genome", "key", "node"))
pair_key <- unique(pairs[, .(genome, key = paste(pmin(dup1, dup2), pmax(dup1, dup2)), type)], by = c("genome", "key"))
cross <- merge(cross, pair_key, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
sd_node <- cross[, .(cross_pairs = .N, classified = sum(!is.na(type)), sd = sum(type == "SD", na.rm = TRUE)), by = node]
sd_node[, sd_share := sd / classified]
nodes <- merge(nodes, sd_node, by = "node", all.x = TRUE)
internal <- merge(internal, sd_node, by = "node", all.x = TRUE)
```

```{r og-genes}
fetch("data/orthofinder/results/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv")
og_tab <- fread("data/orthofinder/results/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = "")
# Genes of each core genome per orthogroup (cells list FASTA headers, ", "-separated)
og_genes <- rbindlist(lapply(gen$genome, function(g) {
  cell <- og_tab[[of_names[[g]]]]
  keep <- cell != ""
  l <- data.table(og = og_tab$Orthogroup[keep], cell = cell[keep])[
    , .(id = sub(" .*", "", unlist(strsplit(cell, ", ", fixed = TRUE)))), by = og]
  a <- alias_all[genome == g]
  unique(l[id %in% a$id][, .(og, genome = g, gene = a$gene[match(id, a$id)])])
}))
og_genes <- merge(og_genes, gmode, by = c("genome", "gene"), all.x = TRUE)
og_genes[is.na(mode), mode := "Not duplicated"]
dup_in_og <- mean(paste(gmode$genome, gmode$gene) %in% paste(og_genes$genome, og_genes$gene))
```

## Neighbourhood synteny

For each paralog pair (A, B), the genes within W genes of A and of B are
compared, ignoring order and orientation. The support of the pair is the
number of other gene families with a paralog pair linking A's window to B's
window. A pair is *neighbourhood-syntenic* if its support reaches k: A and B
lie in regions that were duplicated together with genes of at least k other
families (`r fig("nb_scheme")`). Near-identical pairs were excluded, and pairs
closer than 2W genes on one sequence were not tested. The rate expected by
chance was measured after shuffling gene order in each genome (3 shuffles).
The analysis uses W = 10 and k = 2.

```{r nb-scheme-fig, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.6, fig.cap = cap("nb_scheme", "The neighbourhood synteny test for one paralog pair (A, B), drawn with a window of W = 4 genes (W = 10 in the analysis). Boxes: genes, coloured by gene family; shaded: the window around A and B. Lines: paralog pairs. A link counts as support if it joins A's window to B's window and belongs to another family than A and B. Top: a collinear block, segmental by doubletrouble's rule and neighbourhood-syntenic. Bottom: the same kind of region after gene order has been scrambled; doubletrouble calls A-B dispersed, but three families still link the two windows, so A-B is neighbourhood-syntenic (k = 2). Links of A's own family and links to genes outside a window are not counted.")}
W_demo <- 4; ctr <- 8; n_pos <- 15
p_col <- "Collinear block: segmental in doubletrouble, neighbourhood-syntenic (support = 5 families)"
p_scr <- "Scrambled block: dispersed in doubletrouble, neighbourhood-syntenic (support = 3 families)"
row_genes <- function(fams) {
  f <- rep("Other genes", n_pos)
  for (p in names(fams)) f[as.integer(p)] <- fams[[p]]
  f
}
sch_genes <- rbind(
  data.table(panel = p_col, row = "A", pos = 1:n_pos,
             fam = row_genes(list(`5` = "F1", `6` = "F2", `7` = "F3", `8` = "A/B family", `9` = "F4", `10` = "F5"))),
  data.table(panel = p_col, row = "B", pos = 1:n_pos,
             fam = row_genes(list(`5` = "F1", `6` = "F2", `7` = "F3", `8` = "A/B family", `9` = "F4", `10` = "F5"))),
  data.table(panel = p_scr, row = "A", pos = 1:n_pos,
             fam = row_genes(list(`5` = "F1", `7` = "F2", `8` = "A/B family", `10` = "F3", `11` = "A/B family", `14` = "F4"))),
  data.table(panel = p_scr, row = "B", pos = 1:n_pos,
             fam = row_genes(list(`4` = "F3", `6` = "F1", `8` = "A/B family", `9` = "F4", `11` = "F2", `12` = "A/B family"))))
sch_links <- rbind(
  data.table(panel = p_col, from = c(8, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10), to = c(8, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10),
             kind = c("Focal pair A-B", rep("Supporting link", 5)), fam = c("A/B family", "F1", "F2", "F3", "F4", "F5")),
  data.table(panel = p_scr, from = c(8, 5, 7, 10, 11, 14), to = c(8, 6, 11, 4, 12, 9),
             kind = c("Focal pair A-B", rep("Supporting link", 3), "Not counted", "Not counted"),
             fam = c("A/B family", "F1", "F2", "F3", "A/B family", "F4")))
sch_links[, link_col := fifelse(kind == "Supporting link", fam, kind)]
sch_genes[, y := fifelse(row == "A", 1, 0)]
sch_genes[, label := fifelse(fam == "A/B family" & pos == ctr, row, "")]
fam_fill <- c("A/B family" = "grey20", F1 = "#0072B2", F2 = "#E69F00", F3 = "#009E73",
              F4 = "#CC79A7", F5 = "#56B4E9", "Other genes" = "grey88")
link_cols <- c(fam_fill[c("F1", "F2", "F3", "F4", "F5")], "Focal pair A-B" = "grey20", "Not counted" = "grey60")
panels <- factor(c(p_col, p_scr), c(p_col, p_scr))
sch_genes[, panel := factor(panel, levels(panels))]
sch_links[, panel := factor(panel, levels(panels))]
win <- CJ(panel = panels, y = c(0, 1))
notes <- data.table(panel = factor(p_scr, levels(panels)), x = c(12.3, 15.1), y = c(0.42, 0.62),
                    label = c("own family:\nnot counted", "outside A's\nwindow: not counted"))
ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = win, aes(xmin = ctr - W_demo - 0.5, xmax = ctr + W_demo + 0.5, ymin = y - 0.19, ymax = y + 0.19),
            fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.08) +
  geom_segment(data = sch_links, aes(x = from, xend = to, y = 0.87, yend = 0.13, colour = link_col,
                                     linetype = kind == "Not counted", linewidth = kind == "Focal pair A-B")) +
  geom_tile(data = sch_genes, aes(pos, y, fill = fam), width = 0.78, height = 0.24, colour = "white") +
  geom_text(data = sch_genes, aes(pos, y, label = label), colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  geom_text(data = notes, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 2.8, colour = "grey40", hjust = 0, lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = CJ(panel = panels, y = c(1, 0))[, label := fifelse(y == 1, "region of A", "region of B")],
            aes(x = 0.2, y = y, label = label), hjust = 1, size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(data = data.table(panel = panels), aes(x = ctr, y = 1.3), label = "window: W genes on each side of A and B",
            size = 3, colour = "#0072B2") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = fam_fill, breaks = names(fam_fill), name = "Gene family") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = link_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "solid", `TRUE` = "dashed"), guide = "none") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 0.7, `TRUE` = 1.6), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-1.6, 16.6), ylim = c(-0.3, 1.38), clip = "off") +
  theme_void(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.text = element_text(size = 9.5, face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 4)),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"), plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

```{r nbhd-support}
nb_path <- "data/genome_duplication/neighbourhood_support.tsv.gz"
nb_k <- c(`10` = 2, `20` = 3, `30` = 4)
if (!file.exists(nb_path)) {
  nbhd_support <- function(pp, ord, fam, W) {
    pp <- merge(pp, ord[, .(a = gene, sa = seq, ra = rank)], by = "a")
    pp <- merge(pp, ord[, .(b = gene, sb = seq, rb = rank)], by = "b")
    pp[, `:=`(fam_ab = fam[a], tested = !(sa == sb & abs(ra - rb) <= 2 * W))]
    links <- rbind(pp[, .(x = a, y = b, sx = sa, rx = ra, sy = sb, ry = rb)],
                   pp[, .(x = b, y = a, sx = sb, rx = rb, sy = sa, ry = ra)])
    links[, fam_xy := fam[x]]
    foc <- pp[tested == TRUE, .(a, b, sa, sb, fam_ab, alo = ra - W, ahi = ra + W, blo = rb - W, bhi = rb + W)]
    j <- links[foc, on = .(sx == sa, rx >= alo, rx <= ahi, sy == sb, ry >= blo, ry <= bhi),
               nomatch = NULL, allow.cartesian = TRUE, .(a = i.a, b = i.b, x, y, fam_xy, fam_ab = i.fam_ab)]
    j <- j[x != a & y != b & x != b & y != a & (is.na(fam_xy) | is.na(fam_ab) | fam_xy != fam_ab)]
    j[is.na(fam_xy), fam_xy := paste0("gene:", pmin(x, y))]
    s <- j[, .(support = uniqueN(fam_xy)), by = .(a, b)]
    out <- merge(pp[tested == TRUE, .(a, b)], s, by = c("a", "b"), all.x = TRUE)
    out[is.na(support), support := 0L]
    out
  }
  nb <- rbindlist(lapply(gen$genome, function(g) {
    pp <- pairs[genome == g & !near_ident, .(a = dup1, b = dup2)]
    ord <- unique(gp[genome == g, .(gene = geneID, seq = seqname, start)], by = "gene")
    setorder(ord, seq, start)
    ord[, rank := seq_len(.N), by = seq]
    fam <- og_genes[genome == g, setNames(og, gene)]
    rbindlist(lapply(as.numeric(names(nb_k)), function(W) {
      runs <- list(real = ord)
      for (s in 1:3) { set.seed(s); o <- copy(ord); o[, gene := sample(gene)]; runs[[paste0("null", s)]] <- o }
      rbindlist(lapply(names(runs), function(r) nbhd_support(pp, runs[[r]], fam, W)[, `:=`(W = W, run = r)]))
    }))[, genome := g]
  }))
  fwrite(nb, nb_path, sep = "\t")
}
nb <- fread(nb_path)
nb[, `:=`(key = paste(pmin(a, b), pmax(a, b)), pass = support >= nb_k[as.character(W)], is_null = run != "real")]
nb <- merge(nb, pair_key, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
nb <- merge(nb, gen[, .(genome, order)], by = "genome")
```

```{r nb-calib}
calib <- nb[, .(chance = 100 * mean(pass[is_null]), real = 100 * mean(pass[!is_null]),
                SD = 100 * mean(pass[!is_null & type == "SD"]), DD = 100 * mean(pass[!is_null & type == "DD"])),
            by = .(W, k = nb_k[as.character(W)], order)][order(W, order)]
calib[, DD_over_chance := DD / chance]
num <- c("chance", "real", "SD", "DD", "DD_over_chance")
calib_show <- copy(calib[W == 10])[, (num) := lapply(.SD, function(v) signif(v, 3)), .SDcols = num]
knitr::kable(calib_show, caption = tcap("nb_calib", "Percentage of tested paralog pairs that are neighbourhood-syntenic, by order (window W = 10, threshold k = 2): in genomes with shuffled gene order (chance), in the real genomes (real), and among doubletrouble's segmental (SD) and dispersed (DD) pairs. DD_over_chance: dispersed pairs passing relative to chance."))
```

With shuffled gene order only
`r paste(sprintf("%.2f", range(calib[W == 10, chance])), collapse = "-")`% of
pairs pass, whereas
`r paste(round(range(calib[W == 10 & order != "Umbelopsidales", SD])), collapse = "-")`%
of doubletrouble's segmental pairs in Mortierellales and Mucorales do
(`r tab("nb_calib")`). Among dispersed pairs,
`r sprintf("%.1f", calib[W == 10 & order == "Mucorales", DD])`% pass in
Mucorales and `r sprintf("%.1f", calib[W == 10 & order == "Mortierellales", DD])`%
in Mortierellales, `r round(calib[W == 10 & order == "Mucorales", DD_over_chance])`
and `r round(calib[W == 10 & order == "Mortierellales", DD_over_chance])` times
chance: many dispersed duplicates are eroded segmental duplicates. Wider
windows (W = 20, k = 3; W = 30, k = 4) give the same conclusions.

## Ancestral segmental duplications (ancestral-SD)

A gene-tree duplication is *ancestral-SD* if, in at least two descendant
genomes, one of its pairs is segmental or neighbourhood-syntenic. All its
pairs, in every descendant genome, are then counted as ancestral-SD, including
those that are dispersed today: the duplication arose in a block. Requiring two
genomes keeps chance classifications rare.

```{r nb-nodes}
nbx <- merge(cross[, .(genome, key, node, event)], nb[, .(genome, key, W, run, is_null, pass)],
             by = c("genome", "key"))
nb_node <- nbx[, .(tested = sum(!is_null) / 1, real = 100 * mean(pass[!is_null]), chance = 100 * mean(pass[is_null])),
               by = .(node, W)]
nb_node[, tested := tested]
nb_ev <- nbx[W == 10, .(any = any(pass)), by = .(node, event, run)][
  , .(events = sum(run == "real"), ev_real = 100 * mean(any[run == "real"]), ev_chance = 100 * mean(any[run != "real"])), by = node]
nb_w <- dcast(nb_node, node ~ W, value.var = c("real", "chance", "tested"))
nb_w <- merge(nb_w, nb_ev, by = "node")
nb_w <- merge(nb_w, nodes[, .(node, ntips, clade_order, age_start, age_end)], by = "node")
```

```{r anc-classify}
real10 <- nbx[W == 10 & !is_null]
nb_real10 <- nb[W == 10 & !is_null, .(genome, key, nb_pass = pass)]
anc <- merge(cross[, .(genome, key, node, event, type)], nb_real10, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
anc[, syn := type %in% "SD" | (!is.na(nb_pass) & nb_pass)]
anc <- merge(anc, anc[, .(syn_genomes = uniqueN(genome[syn])), by = event], by = "event")
anc[, cls := fcase(syn_genomes >= 2, "Ancestral-SD", syn_genomes == 1, "Syntenic in 1 genome",
                   default = "No synteny")]
anc[cls == "Ancestral-SD", cls := "ancientSD"]   # internal name used by the shared code below
pair_ks <- unique(pairs[, .(genome, key = paste(pmin(dup1, dup2), pmax(dup1, dup2)), Ks)], by = c("genome", "key"))
anc <- merge(anc, pair_ks, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
ev_cls <- unique(anc[, .(event, node, cls)])
# chance rate of ancestral-SD: the same rule applied to the shuffled genomes
ev_null <- nbx[W == 10 & is_null, .(n_genomes = uniqueN(genome[pass])), by = .(node, event, run)]
```

```{r anc-branches-fig, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = cap("anc_branches", "Gene-tree duplications on key branches, by synteny class: ancestral-SD (segmental or neighbourhood-syntenic in at least two descendant genomes), syntenic in one genome, or no synteny. Numbers: ancestral-SD duplications and their share. The Absidia and Rhizopus branches carry recent WGDs (Section 5).")}
bk <- ev_cls[node %in% key_nodes$node, .N, by = .(node, cls)]
bk <- merge(bk, key_nodes, by = "node")
bk[, `:=`(lab = factor(paste0(label, " (", node, ")"), rev(paste0(key_nodes$label, " (", key_nodes$node, ")"))),
          cls = factor(cls, rev(c("ancientSD", "Syntenic in 1 genome", "No synteny")),
                       rev(c("Ancestral-SD", "Syntenic in 1 genome", "No synteny"))))]
bk_tot <- bk[, .(total = sum(N), anc = sum(N[cls == "Ancestral-SD"])), by = lab]
ggplot(bk, aes(N, lab, fill = cls)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(data = bk_tot, aes(x = total, y = lab, label = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", fmt_n(anc), 100 * anc / total)),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Ancestral-SD" = "#D55E00", "Syntenic in 1 genome" = "#F0B27A", "No synteny" = "grey80"),
                    breaks = c("Ancestral-SD", "Syntenic in 1 genome", "No synteny"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(x = "Gene-tree duplications (at least 50% support)", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r anc-counts}
stems <- key_nodes[, .(node, stem = paste0(label, " (", node, ")"))]
ac <- anc[node %in% stems$node]
ac_ev <- unique(ac[, .(node, event, cls)])[, .(duplications = .N, ancientSD = sum(cls == "ancientSD")), by = node]
ac_sd <- ac[cls == "ancientSD"]
ac_genes <- ac_sd[, .(genes = uniqueN(c(paste(genome, sub(" .*", "", key)), paste(genome, sub(".* ", "", key)))),
                      genomes = uniqueN(genome), pairs = .N, classified = sum(!is.na(type)),
                      SD = sum(type %in% "SD"), TD = sum(type %in% "TD"), PD = sum(type %in% "PD"),
                      DD = sum(type %in% "DD")), by = node]
anc_counts <- merge(stems, merge(ac_ev, ac_genes, by = "node"), by = "node", sort = FALSE)
anc_counts[, chance := vapply(node, function(nd) 100 * ev_null[node == nd, mean(n_genomes >= 2)], 0)]
anc_counts_show <- anc_counts[, .(
  branch = stem, `supported duplications` = fmt_n(duplications),
  `ancestral-SD duplications` = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", fmt_n(ancientSD), 100 * ancientSD / duplications),
  `chance (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", chance),
  `descendant genes` = sprintf("%s (%d genomes)", fmt_n(genes), genomes),
  `copy pairs` = fmt_n(pairs), classified = fmt_n(classified),
  SD = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", fmt_n(SD), 100 * SD / classified),
  TD = fmt_n(TD), PD = fmt_n(PD),
  DD = sprintf("%s (%.0f%%)", fmt_n(DD), 100 * DD / classified))]
knitr::kable(anc_counts_show, caption = tcap("anc_counts", "Ancestral-SD duplications on key branches. Supported duplications: OrthoFinder gene-tree duplications on the branch with at least 50% support. Chance: % of duplications classified ancestral-SD after shuffling gene order. Descendant genes: present-day copies descending from the ancestral-SD duplications, summed over genomes. Copy pairs: pairs of copies from the two sides of each duplication within a genome; classified: pairs that doubletrouble classified (the others were not among either gene's top 5 within-genome DIAMOND hits), with their current mode (% of classified pairs)."))
```

```{r nb-events-fig, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = cap("nb_events", "Mucorales-stem duplications across Mucorales genomes. Left: number of genomes in which a Mucorales-stem duplication has a neighbourhood-syntenic pair, for the real genomes and with shuffled gene order (mean of 3 shuffles); duplications syntenic in no genome are not shown. Right: neighbourhood-syntenic pairs (%) among the Mucorales-stem duplicates in each Mucorales genome, in species-tree order.")}

```{r anc-values}
ac <- function(nd, col) anc_counts[node == nd][[col]]
anc_pct <- function(nd) round(100 * ac(nd, "ancientSD") / ac(nd, "duplications"))
null_anc <- function(nd) 100 * ev_null[node == nd, mean(n_genomes >= 2)]
top_g <- g12[order(-pct)][1:3]
gname <- function(g) gen$species[match(g, gen$genome)]
```

`r fmt_n(ac("N12", "ancientSD"))` of the `r fmt_n(ac("N12", "duplications"))`
Mucorales-stem duplications (`r anc_pct("N12")`%; `r sprintf("%.1f", null_anc("N12"))`%
expected with shuffled gene order) and `r fmt_n(ac("N10", "ancientSD"))` of the
`r fmt_n(ac("N10", "duplications"))` Mortierellales-stem duplications
(`r anc_pct("N10")`%) are ancestral-SD (`r fig("anc_branches")`,
`r tab("anc_counts")`). The preceding branch, shared with Umbelopsidales
(N9), carries fewer duplications although it is longer
(`r fmt_n(ac("N9", "duplications"))`, of which `r anc_pct("N9")`% ancestral-SD;
`r sprintf("%.1f", null_anc("N9"))`% expected by chance), and the root of
Mucoromycota only `r ac("N8", "duplications")`
(`r ac("N8", "ancientSD")` ancestral-SD).
The Mucorales-stem ancestral-SD duplications have
`r fmt_n(ac("N12", "genes"))` descendant genes in `r ac("N12", "genomes")`
genomes; `r round(100 * ac("N12", "DD") / ac("N12", "classified"))`% of their
classified pairs are dispersed today, against
`r round(100 * ac("N10", "DD") / ac("N10", "classified"))`% on the
Mortierellales stem. The same duplication is often syntenic in some Mucorales
genomes and dispersed in the rest; synteny survives best in
`r paste(sprintf("*%s* (%.0f%%)", gname(top_g$genome), top_g$pct), collapse = ", ")`
(`r fig("nb_events")`).

# Ks of segmental and ancestral-segmental duplicates

Ks grows with the age of a duplicate pair until it saturates at about 2. A
large-scale duplication leaves many pairs of the same age, a peak in the Ks
distribution, as long as it is younger than saturation.

```{r ks-data}
ksd <- pairs[!near_ident & Ks <= 5]
ksd[, class := fifelse(type == "SD", "Segmental (SD)", "Small-scale (TD, PD, DD)")]
ksd <- merge(ksd, gen[, .(genome, genes, order)], by = "genome")
```

```{r ks-heat-fig, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 10, fig.cap = cap("ks_heat", "Ks distributions of segmental pairs per genome, in species-tree order. Colour: pairs per 1,000 genes in each Ks bin (log-spaced bins, square-root scale; white: no pairs). Near-identical pairs excluded. Dashed line: Ks = 2.")}
breaks <- seq(log10(0.05), log10(5), length.out = 41)
ksd[, bin := cut(log10(Ks), breaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)]
heat <- ksd[, .(n = .N), by = .(genome, class, bin, genes)]
heat[, per_1k := 1000 * n / genes]
heat[, `:=`(x = (breaks[bin] + breaks[bin + 1]) / 2, genome = factor(genome, tip_order))]
heat_panel <- function(cl, show_y = TRUE) {
  ggplot(heat[class == cl], aes(x, genome, fill = per_1k)) +
    geom_tile() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = log10(2), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey40") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = log10(c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5)),
                       labels = c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "sqrt", name = "Pairs per\n1,000 genes") +
    labs(x = "Ks", y = NULL, title = cl) +
    theme(axis.text.y = if (show_y) element_text(size = 7) else element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = if (show_y) element_line() else element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5))
}
heat_panel("Segmental (SD)")
```

Peaks were fitted with Gaussian mixture models on log Ks (Ks 0.05-5, 1-4
components chosen by BIC) for genomes with at least 100 segmental pairs, so
that the saturated pairs form their own component (`r tab("peaks")`). To place
peaks relative to speciation, Ks was computed in the same way for 400 random
one-to-one orthologs of species pairs bracketing the candidate events
(`r tab("orthks")`): a peak with a lower Ks than the orthologs of two species
arose after their split.

```{r ks-peaks}
fit_peaks <- function(ks) {
  m <- densityMclust(log(ks), G = 1:4, modelNames = "V", verbose = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
  o <- order(m$parameters$mean)
  data.table(component = seq_along(o), mean_log = m$parameters$mean[o],
             sd_log = sqrt(m$parameters$variance$sigmasq[o]), weight = m$parameters$pro[o])
}
sd_n <- ksd[class == "Segmental (SD)", .N, by = genome]
peak_genomes <- intersect(tip_order, sd_n[N >= 100, genome])
peaks <- rbindlist(lapply(peak_genomes, function(g) {
  fit_peaks(ksd[genome == g & class == "Segmental (SD)", Ks])[, genome := g]
}))
peaks[, Ks := exp(mean_log)]
# The main sub-saturation peak: the largest component with mean Ks < 2
main_peak <- peaks[Ks < 2][order(-weight)][, .SD[1], by = genome]
peak_tab <- peaks[, .(components = paste(sprintf("%.2f (%.0f%%)", Ks, 100 * weight), collapse = ", ")),
                  by = genome]
peak_tab <- merge(peak_tab, sd_n, by = "genome")
peak_tab <- merge(peak_tab, main_peak[, .(genome, main_Ks = round(Ks, 2), main_weight = round(weight, 2))],
                  by = "genome", all.x = TRUE)
peak_tab <- merge(gen[, .(genome, order)], peak_tab, by = "genome")[order(order, -main_weight)]
knitr::kable(peak_tab[, .(genome, order, SD_pairs = N, components, main_Ks, main_weight)],
             caption = tcap("peaks", "Gaussian mixture components of the log-Ks distribution of segmental pairs (Ks 0.05-5): component mean Ks and weight. main_Ks and main_weight: the largest component with mean Ks < 2."))
```

```{r ortholog-ks}
orth_pairs <- data.table(
  a = c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "AbsRepe", "ggRhiOryz1", "ggRhiOryz1", "AbsRepe",
        "ggMorZona1", "ggRhiOryz1", "ggRhiOryz1"),
  b = c("AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1", "HalRadi", "gzRhiStol1", "gzRhiMicr1", "ggRhiOryz1",
        "gzPodHuml1", "gzUmbVina1", "ggMorZona1"),
  split = c("Within Absidia (A. cylindrospora / A. repens)", "Within Absidia (A. repens / A. glauca)",
            "Absidia / Halteromyces", "Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. stolonifer)",
            "Within Rhizopus (R. oryzae / R. microsporus)", "Absidia / Rhizopus",
            "Mortierellales crown", "Mucorales / Umbelopsidales", "Mucorales / Mortierellales"))

orth_path <- "data/genome_duplication/ortholog_ks.tsv"
if (!file.exists(orth_path)) {
  load_cds <- function(g) {
    f <- sprintf("data/doubletrouble/input_data/%s_data.rds", gen[genome == g, dt_id])
    fetch(f)
    cds <- readRDS(f)$cds
    cds[Biostrings::width(cds) %% 3 == 0]  # as in pairs2kaks()
  }
  load_alias <- function(g) {  # any OrthoFinder identifier -> gene ID
    f <- sprintf("data/genomes/%1$s/%1$s_IDtbl.tsv", g)
    fetch(f)
    ids <- fread(f)
    unique(rbind(ids[, .(id = proteinID, gene = geneID)], ids[, .(id = rnaID, gene = geneID)],
                 ids[, .(id = geneID, gene = geneID)]))
  }
  # OrthoFinder separates genes with ", "; public FASTA headers carry descriptions,
  # so take the first word of each element that is a known identifier.
  known_id <- function(cell, known) {
    vapply(strsplit(cell, ", ", fixed = TRUE), function(p) {
      w <- sub(" .*", "", p); w <- w[w %in% known]
      if (length(w) == 1) w else NA_character_
    }, "")
  }
  n_genes_in <- function(cell) lengths(strsplit(cell, ", ", fixed = TRUE))
  ks_of_pairs <- function(cds_a, cds_b, ga, gb) {
    seqs <- c(cds_a[ga], cds_b[gb])
    names(seqs) <- c(paste0("a_", ga), paste0("b_", gb))
    idx <- lapply(seq_along(ga), function(i) c(i, length(ga) + i))
    r <- MSA2dist::indices2kaks(cds = seqs, indices = idx, model = "MYN", isMSA = FALSE,
                                threads = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1), verbose = FALSE)
    as.numeric(ifelse(r$Ks == "NA", NA, r$Ks))
  }
  ortholog_ks <- function(a, b, n = 400, seed = 1) {
    f <- sprintf("data/orthofinder/results/Orthologues/Orthologues_%1$s/%1$s__v__%2$s.tsv",
                 of_names[[a]], of_names[[b]])
    fetch(f)
    o <- fread(f, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, quote = "", col.names = c("og", "a", "b"))
    alias_a <- load_alias(a); alias_b <- load_alias(b)
    one <- o[n_genes_in(a) == 1 & n_genes_in(b) == 1]
    one[, `:=`(gene_a = alias_a$gene[match(known_id(a, alias_a$id), alias_a$id)],
               gene_b = alias_b$gene[match(known_id(b, alias_b$id), alias_b$id)])]
    cds_a <- load_cds(a); cds_b <- load_cds(b)
    one <- one[gene_a %in% names(cds_a) & gene_b %in% names(cds_b)]
    set.seed(seed)
    s <- one[sample(.N, min(n, .N))]
    data.table(a = a, b = b, one_to_one = nrow(one), gene_a = s$gene_a, gene_b = s$gene_b,
               Ks = ks_of_pairs(cds_a, cds_b, s$gene_a, s$gene_b))
  }
  orth_ks <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(orth_pairs)), function(i) {
    ortholog_ks(orth_pairs$a[i], orth_pairs$b[i])
  }))
  fwrite(orth_ks, orth_path, sep = "\t")
}
orth_ks <- fread(orth_path)
orth_ks <- merge(orth_ks, orth_pairs, by = c("a", "b"))
orth_sum <- orth_ks[, .(one_to_one = one_to_one[1], sampled = .N,
                        Ks_q25 = quantile(Ks, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), Ks_median = median(Ks, na.rm = TRUE),
                        Ks_q75 = quantile(Ks, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
                        saturated_pct = 100 * mean(Ks > 2, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(split, a, b)]
orth_sum <- orth_sum[match(orth_pairs$split, split)]
num <- c("Ks_q25", "Ks_median", "Ks_q75", "saturated_pct")
orth_sum[, (num) := lapply(.SD, round, 2), .SDcols = num]
knitr::kable(orth_sum, caption = tcap("orthks", "Ks between one-to-one orthologs of species pairs (400 random orthologs per pair; MYN model, as for the paralogs). one_to_one: number of one-to-one orthologs available. saturated_pct: percentage of orthologs with Ks > 2."))
```

```{r anc-ks-summary}
nb_real10 <- nb[W == 10 & !is_null, .(genome, key, nb_pass = pass)]
anc <- merge(cross[, .(genome, key, node, event, type)], nb_real10, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
anc[, syn := type %in% "SD" | (!is.na(nb_pass) & nb_pass)]
anc <- merge(anc, anc[, .(syn_genomes = uniqueN(genome[syn])), by = event], by = "event")
anc[, cls := fcase(syn_genomes >= 2, "ancientSD", syn_genomes == 1, "Syntenic in 1 genome",
                   default = "No synteny")]
pair_ks <- unique(pairs[, .(genome, key = paste(pmin(dup1, dup2), pmax(dup1, dup2)), Ks)], by = c("genome", "key"))
anc <- merge(anc, pair_ks, by = c("genome", "key"), all.x = TRUE)
anc_nodes <- key_nodes[node != "N8"]
anc_ev <- unique(anc[, .(event, node, cls)])[node %in% anc_nodes$node,
  .(events = .N, ancientSD = sum(cls == "ancientSD")), by = node]
ksw <- anc[node %in% anc_nodes$node & !is.na(Ks) & Ks >= 0.05 & Ks <= 5]
ksw[, set := fifelse(cls == "ancientSD", "ancientSD", "other")]
anc_ks <- ksw[, .(pairs = .N, median_Ks = median(Ks), below2 = 100 * mean(Ks < 2),
                  window = 100 * mean(Ks > 1.5 & Ks < 2.6)), by = .(node, set)]
anc_ks_w <- dcast(anc_ks, node ~ set, value.var = c("pairs", "median_Ks", "below2", "window"))
anc_tab <- merge(anc_nodes, merge(anc_ev, anc_ks_w, by = "node"), by = "node", sort = FALSE)
anc_show <- anc_tab[, .(node, label, events, ancientSD_pct = round(100 * ancientSD / events),
                        ancientSD_pairs = pairs_ancientSD, median_Ks = round(median_Ks_ancientSD, 2),
                        Ks_below_2 = round(below2_ancientSD, 1),
                        Ks_1.5_2.6 = round(window_ancientSD, 1), Ks_1.5_2.6_other = round(window_other, 1))]
knitr::kable(anc_show, caption = tcap("anc", "Gene-tree duplications that are ancestral-SD (segmental or neighbourhood-syntenic in at least two descendant genomes) on key branches, and the Ks of their duplicate pairs (Ks 0.05-5). Ks_below_2: % of ancestral-SD pairs with Ks < 2; Ks_1.5_2.6: % between Ks 1.5 and 2.6 (the Mortierellales Ks component), for ancestral-SD pairs and for the other pairs of the same branch."))

```{r ks-values}
mp <- function(g) main_peak[genome == g]
om <- function(s) orth_sum[split == s, Ks_median]
abs_rhi <- c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1", "ggRhiOryz1")
mort_mid <- peaks[genome %in% gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome] & Ks > 1.5 & Ks < 3]
av <- function(nd, col) anc_show[node == nd][[col]]
deep_sat <- orth_sum[split %in% c("Mucorales / Umbelopsidales", "Mucorales / Mortierellales"), range(Ks_median)]
gl_pre <- paste0(gsub(".", "_", of_names[["gzAbsGlau1"]], fixed = TRUE), "_")
has_gla <- function(x) vapply(strsplit(x, ", ", fixed = TRUE), function(v) any(startsWith(v, gl_pre)), FALSE)
gla_both <- function(nd) round(100 * sup[node == nd, mean(has_gla(genes1) & has_gla(genes2))])
```

- ***Absidia* and *Rhizopus*.** Their segmental pairs have a main Ks
  component at `r paste(sprintf("%.2f", range(main_peak[genome %in% abs_rhi, Ks])), collapse = "-")`
  holding `r paste(pct(range(main_peak[genome %in% abs_rhi, weight])), collapse = "-")`%
  of the pairs (`r fig("ks_heat")`, `r tab("peaks")`), and their ancestral-SD
  duplicates have a median Ks of `r av("N46", "median_Ks")` and
  `r av("N32", "median_Ks")` (`r fig("anc_ks")`). Both events are younger than
  the split of the two genera (ortholog Ks `r om("Absidia / Rhizopus")`), so
  they are independent. The gene trees place the *Rhizopus* event before the
  split of *R. oryzae* and *R. stolonifer*.
- **One *Absidia* WGD, partly rediploidized after a speciation.** The *Absidia*
  duplications fall on two branches, before and after *A. glauca* diverged
  (`r fig("anc_branches")`). *A. glauca* has both copies of
  `r gla_both("N40")`% of the duplications placed before its split, so these
  are shared. It lies outside the duplications placed after its split, but in
  many of these families its own copies form a separate duplication on the
  *A. glauca* branch, and these pairs are younger (median Ks of ancestral-SD
  pairs `r av("N46", "median_Ks")` against `r av("N40", "median_Ks")`). This
  is the pattern of a single WGD whose rediploidization was completed for part
  of the genome only after the speciation (lineage-specific ohnolog
  resolution, as after the salmonid WGD), not of a second round; *A. glauca*
  has also lost more copies or has a less complete annotation (details in the
  extended report).
- **Mortierellales.** All `r uniqueN(mort_mid$genome)` Mortierellales genomes
  have a segmental Ks component at
  `r paste(sprintf("%.1f", range(mort_mid$Ks)), collapse = "-")`, and the
  ancestral-SD pairs of the Mortierellales stem are enriched in this range
  (`r av("N10", "Ks_1.5_2.6")`% between Ks 1.5 and 2.6, against
  `r av("N10", "Ks_1.5_2.6_other")`% for the other stem duplicates).
- **Mucorales stem.** Its ancestral-SD pairs are saturated (median Ks
  `r av("N12", "median_Ks")`; `r av("N12", "Ks_below_2")`% below 2), as is the
  divergence between the orders (median ortholog Ks
  `r paste(sprintf("%.1f", deep_sat), collapse = "-")`), so Ks cannot date this
  event.

# Conclusions {-}

```{r summary-fig, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = cap("summary", "Summary of the large-scale duplication events on the dated species tree (relative time, root = 1,000). Clades without an event are collapsed into triangles (number of genomes in brackets). Numbered markers sit on the branches where the gene trees place the duplications; filled markers are events with block (ancestral-SD) and Ks evidence, the open marker a weaker block signal.")}
# Collapsed clades, defined on the full tree
grp <- data.table(
  name = c("Mortierellales", "Umbelopsidales", "Lichtheimia and relatives", "Phycomyces, Radiomyces",
           "Cunninghamella", "Mucor and relatives", "Rhizopus microsporus"),
  tips = list(gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome], gen[order == "Umbelopsidales", genome],
              c("gzLicCory1", "SynRace"), c("PhyBlak1", "RadSpec"), c("CunBert", "gzCunBlak1", "gzCunEchi1"),
              c("gzMucCirc1", "MycAfri"), c("gzRhiMicr1", "RhiMicr2")),
  col = c(order_cols[["Mortierellales"]], order_cols[["Umbelopsidales"]], rep(order_cols[["Mucorales"]], 5)))
grp[, members := lapply(tips, function(tl) extract.clade(tree, getMRCA(tree, tl))$tip.label)]
grp[, n := lengths(members)]
# Display tree: two genomes per collapsed clade, one from each side of its root,
# so every triangle keeps its depth but takes the same space
rep_tips <- function(tl) {
  m <- getMRCA(tree, tl)
  vapply(tree$edge[tree$edge[, 1] == m, 2],
         function(ch) if (ch <= Ntip(tree)) tree$tip.label[ch] else extract.clade(tree, ch)$tip.label[1], "")
}
grp[, reps := lapply(tips, rep_tips)]
keep <- data.table(genome = c("HalRadi", "gzAbsGlau1", "gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "ggRhiOryz1", "gzRhiStol1"))
stree <- keep.tip(tree, c(unlist(grp$reps), keep$genome))
mrca <- function(tips) getMRCA(stree, intersect(tips, stree$tip.label))
grp[, node := vapply(reps, mrca, 0L)]
p0 <- ggtree(stree, ladderize = TRUE)
d0 <- as.data.table(p0$data)
grp[, y := vapply(reps, function(tl) mean(d0[label %in% tl, y]), 0)]
p <- p0
for (i in seq_len(nrow(grp))) {
  p <- collapse(p, grp$node[i], mode = "mixed", fill = grp$col[i], colour = grp$col[i], alpha = 0.35)
}
keep[, `:=`(y = d0$y[match(genome, d0$label)], species = gen$species[match(genome, gen$genome)])]
ev <- data.table(
  id = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"),
  node = c(mrca(gen[order == "Mucorales", genome]), mrca(gen[order == "Mortierellales", genome]),
           mrca(c("AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1")),
           mrca(c("ggRhiOryz1", "gzRhiStol1")), mrca(gen[order != "Mortierellales", genome])),
  strong = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
ev[, `:=`(x = d0$branch[match(node, d0$node)], y = d0$y[match(node, d0$node)])]
ev_col <- "#D55E00"
p_tree <- p +
  geom_tiplab(data = function(d) d[d$label %in% keep$genome, ], aes(label = gen$species[match(label, gen$genome)]),
              fontface = "italic", size = 3.2, offset = 12) +
  geom_text(data = grp, aes(x = 1012, y = y, label = sprintf("%s (%d)", name, n)), hjust = 0, size = 3.3,
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_point(data = ev, aes(x, y, fill = strong), shape = 21, size = 7, colour = ev_col, stroke = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = ev, aes(x, y, label = id, colour = strong), size = 3.6, fontface = "bold", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = ev_col, `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = ev_col), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-10, 1330), clip = "off") +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5))
# Evidence per event
abs_ks <- main_peak[genome %in% c("gzAbsCyli1", "AbsRepe", "gzAbsGlau1"), median(Ks)]
rhi_ks <- main_peak[genome == "ggRhiOryz1", Ks]
ev_txt <- data.table(
  id = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "5"), strong = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE),
  title = c("Mucorales stem: ancient large-scale duplication", "Mortierellales stem: large-scale duplication",
            "Absidia: recent WGD, before the A. glauca split", "Rhizopus oryzae + R. stolonifer: recent WGD",
            "Umbelopsidales + Mucorales stem: weaker block signal"),
  text = c(sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications (%d%%) in %d genomes; blocks eroded (%d%% dispersed today); Ks saturated",
                   fmt_n(ac("N12", "ancientSD")), anc_pct("N12"), ac("N12", "genomes"),
                   round(100 * ac("N12", "DD") / ac("N12", "classified"))),
           sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications (%d%%); collinear blocks partly retained; Ks component %.1f-%.1f",
                   fmt_n(ac("N10", "ancientSD")), anc_pct("N10"), min(mort_mid$Ks), max(mort_mid$Ks)),
           sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications; Ks peak %.1f; rediploidization partly completed after the A. glauca split (LORe-like)",
                   fmt_n(ac("N40", "ancientSD") + ac("N46", "ancientSD")), abs_ks),
           sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications; Ks peak %.1f; after the split from R. microsporus",
                   fmt_n(ac("N32", "ancientSD")), rhi_ks),
           sprintf("%s ancestral-SD duplications (%d%%); possibly Mucorales-stem duplications placed too deep",
                   fmt_n(ac("N9", "ancientSD")), anc_pct("N9"))))
ev_txt[, row := rev(seq_len(.N))]
p_txt <- ggplot(ev_txt) +
  geom_point(aes(0, row, fill = strong), shape = 21, size = 7, colour = ev_col, stroke = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(0, row, label = id, colour = strong), size = 3.6, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(aes(0.06, row + 0.14, label = title), hjust = 0, fontface = "bold", size = 3.3) +
  geom_text(aes(0.06, row - 0.02, label = stringr::str_wrap(text, 62)), hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 2.9,
            lineheight = 0.95, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = ev_col, `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = ev_col), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.03, 1)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.2, nrow(ev_txt) + 0.5)) +
  theme_void()
p_tree + p_txt + plot_layout(widths = c(1.35, 1))
```

- **An ancient large-scale duplication shared by all Mucorales.**
  `r fmt_n(ac("N12", "ancientSD"))` gene-tree duplications on the Mucorales
  stem arose in duplicated blocks; their copies survive in
  `r ac("N12", "genomes")` of the 42 Mucorales genomes but are now mostly
  dispersed, because gene order has been scrambled since. The event is older
  than Ks can resolve. The signal is concentrated on the Mucorales stem: the
  branch shared with Umbelopsidales and the root of Mucoromycota carry fewer
  duplications and a smaller share of ancestral-SD ones, so the event most
  likely postdates the split from Umbelopsidales; some of the signal on the
  shared branch may be Mucorales-stem duplications placed one branch too deep
  by gene-tree errors. This matches, and places more precisely, the WGD
  proposed by Corrochano et al. (2016).
- **Lineage-specific large-scale duplications.** Two recent, independent
  events in *Absidia* and *Rhizopus* (Ks about 1.6-1.9), with many collinear
  blocks still intact; and an event on the Mortierellales stem
  (`r fmt_n(ac("N10", "ancientSD"))` ancestral-SD duplications) whose Ks
  component near 2.4 suggests it is younger than the Mucorales-stem event.
- **WGD or several segmental duplications.** These analyses show block
  duplications on each branch but cannot tell a single WGD from several large
  segmental duplications. A model-based test (Whale) is planned.
